newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea's Kim to reshuffle govt -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: North Korea's Kim to reshuffle govt -- newspaper.

text.p: North Korea's Kim Jong-il is set to reshuffle his government after the official mourning period of his late father Kim Il-sung ends next week, a Japanese newspaper reported on Saturday.

Citing diplomatic sources in Tokyo, the ultra-conservative daily Sankei Shimbun said Kim was preparing to fill in key government and military posts with close aides before officially assuming his father's posts.
Stalinist North Korea next week marks the end of the traditional three-year mourning period for the late Kim Il-sung.
Although junior Kim has been in control of the state since his father's death, the general secretary post of the ruling Worker's Party and state presidency have been left vacant.

The newspaper said Kim was likely to appoint Jo Myong-rok defence minister, vacant since Choe Kwang died in February. Jo is currently the military's general political bureau director and accompanies Kim whenever he visits the troops.
Other likely appointments included current Foreign Minister Kim Yong-nam as vice president, and Kang Sok-ju as foreign minister, the daily said.

Sankei also said Kim was likely to assume the state presidency on September 9, North Korea's foundation day, and separately take up the party post around October 10, the founding anniversary of the party.
